papers.summary: On the real hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, the classical Muckenhoupt condition does not describe the weights $w$ for which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$. We show that, for $1<p<\infty$, $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$ if and only if $w$ is a local $A_p$ weight and satisfies a two-layer condition, which compares $w$ and its dual weight on two layers of the shadow of a point. We also treat the weak type case, radial weights and the range $p\le1$, and we prove a weighted Herz principle for radial convolution operators.
papers.title: Muckenhoupt weights for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on hyperbolic spaces

papers.summary: We determine the dimension-independent first-order query complexity of minimizing a Lipschitz geodesically convex (g-convex) function on hyperbolic space. Given a ball of radius $r$ containing a global minimizer, we prove that $Ω(ζ_r/ε^2)$ queries are necessary to attain accuracy $εMr$, where $M$ is the Lipschitz constant and $ζ_r=r/\tanh r$ captures the effect of curvature. This matches the known $O(ζ_r/ε^2)$ upper bound for the Riemannian subgradient method (Zhang and Sra, 2016). This is the first query-complexity result for g-convex optimization that is tight simultaneously in curvature and target accuracy. The standard Euclidean recipe of constructing hard instances as maxima of affine functions does not transfer to hyperbolic space, so the lower bound requires a new mechanism. Our starting point is the worst-function construction of Criscitiello and Boumal (2023, Appendix A). It gives the same lower bound for a subclass of algorithms, including the subgradient method, whose queries remain in prescribed g-convex regions. We retain this geometric setup and carefully tune and augment their hard function to accommodate every deterministic first-order algorithm. The key new mechanism is an advance-or-stall scheme: when a query lies in these regions, the oracle reveals at most one new information direction (advance); when a query leaves them, we show that the oracle can answer without revealing any new hidden direction (stall). Unlike earlier curvature-dependent lower bounds, the proof uses no ball-packing argument.
papers.title: Tight lower bounds for Lipschitz geodesically convex optimization on hyperbolic space

papers.summary: The water removal from refractory castables is a complex process involving heat and mass transport and thermohygromechanical stresses. In order to reduce the risk of explosive spalling by improving the heat-up curves, numerical models are critical to predict the castable behavior during drying. However, most of the existing models either neglect the thermomechanical stresses or consider them as an \textit{a posteriori} assessment of the likelihood of failure. The present work proposes an open-source thermohygromechanical phase-field model to simulate the drying of refractory castables and predict the occurrence of explosive spalling. The model is based on an adaptive two-scale time-stepping strategy that allows for a significant reduction of the computational cost associated with the simulation. The model was validated against literature results and qualitative comparisons with experimental data were carried out to assess its ability to predict the failure behavior of partially saturated porous media during heating. The numerical simulations were also applied to investigate the impact of different heating methods on the risk of failure during drying. It was found that even at the significantly lower heating rates typical of refractory castable drying - compared to the fire accidents that motivate most thermomechanical studies on concrete structures - thermomechanical stresses still play a significant role in the explosive spalling, a finding well established for concrete under fire but novel for refractory castables. As a consequence, it was also concluded that the use of heterogeneous heating methods can increase the likelihood of explosive spalling. Ultimately, feasible solutions to increase the drying efficiency and safety that are compatible with the industrial setting were proposed and a free, open-source implementation of the model is provided.
papers.title: An Efficient Open-Source Framework for Thermohygromechanical Phase-Field Simulation of Drying Damage Refractory Castables

papers.summary: We present a boundary integral method for evaluating electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) in dielectric environments of piecewise constant permittivity. This generalizes conventional bare-Coulomb ERIs by incorporating screening from structured dielectric surroundings, such as the substrates and/or encapsulating layers present in modern two-dimensional-material devices. We formulate the problem as a second-kind boundary integral equation for the induced surface charge on the dielectric interfaces, and discretize it with a Nyström method on adaptively refined panels. The incident potential generated by each smooth orbital source density is evaluated by a Fourier truncated-kernel method in or near to its source box, and by fast multipole method (FMM) accelerated quadrature farther away. The linear system is solved by a Krylov iteration also accelerated by the FMM. We focus on cuboidal device geometries, and retain efficiency at high aspect ratios via close-to-touching panel quadratures. We further develop a distributed pipeline that computes the full ERI tensor, comprising thousands of orbital pairs, embedded in a single dielectric geometry. We demonstrate the method on an effective three-layer graphene slab over a Si/SiO$_2$ heterojunction, focusing on the central graphene layer represented by $198$ $p_z$-like orbitals, retaining the $2613^2$ non-negligible entries of the $198^4$-sized ERI tensor. The model is resolved on $1.3$ million surface unknowns, achieving a relative error of $0.004\%$, at a cost of $22$ node-hours.
papers.title: A boundary integral method for computing electron repulsion integrals in heterogeneous dielectric environments

papers.summary: Muon, a 2024-born optimizer for language models, differs from the 2015-born spectral gradient descent mainly in its fast, GPU-friendly Newton--Schulz polynomial for orthogonalizing the gradient matrix. Accordingly, a line of research proposes faster polynomial iterations for gradient orthogonalization, such as Polar Express and Gram Newton--Schulz, both built on quintic polynomials. In this paper, we introduce Polar Switch, a new approach to polynomial gradient orthogonalization. Using simple polynomial circuits, Polar Switch reaches a given high polynomial degree at a lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations. We define a circuit as a short sequence of symmetric matrix products on a few square buffers, and circuits with $k$ products form a restricted family of odd polynomials of degree up to $2^{k+1}+1$. We choose the sequence of products in each circuit, their coefficients, and how the circuits are composed by numerically minimizing a worst-case bound on the polar approximation error. This minimization is subject to a FLOP budget that accounts for symmetric matrix multiplication kernels and a rounding constraint for numerical stability in half precision. Our two recommended Polar Switch methods have 15.5--18.7\% lower runtime than Polar Express on square matrices and 8.6--16.2\% lower runtime than Gram Newton--Schulz on rectangular matrices with aspect ratios 3.25, 3.5, and 8, with comparable approximation accuracy. In pretraining Modded-NanoGPT \#91, Qwen3-0.6B, and Gemma 3-1B, Polar Switch reaches final validation losses similar to those of established orthogonalization methods. Across the more than 14 million matrices that each of the two recommended methods orthogonalized in these runs, the estimated output spectral norms never exceed the designed bounds by more than 3\%, demonstrating their numerical stability.
papers.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits

papers.summary: Let $P$ be a trigonometric polynomial with only real zeros. We prove that at most $\frac{2}{3}$ of its zeros coincide with the zeros of the Riemann zeta function $ζ(s)$ on the critical line. We also show that \begin{equation*} \sup_{\substack{T\leq x\leq2T\\ P(x)=0}} \log \left|ζ\left(\frac{1}{2}+ix\right)\right| \geq (1+o(1))\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{6\log\log T}}. \end{equation*} These results extend the corresponding theorems of Li and Radziwill on the zeros of $ζ(s)$ along vertical arithmetic progressions. The main novelty in our approach is the use of the work of Kurasov and Sarnak and Lee-Yang representations of Alon-Cohen-Vinzant, which show that the corresponding measure $\sum_{P(γ)=0} {\bf δ}_γ$ is crystalline.
papers.title: The Riemann zeta function at the zeros of real-rooted trigonometric polynomials

papers.summary: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=wλ$ for real or octonion $λ$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(wλ_1)λ_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $λ_2λ_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.
papers.title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator

papers.summary: A stabilized semi-discrete finite element scheme for the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system is presented. The scheme uses the Whitney $2$-form and $1$-form for the fluid velocity and magnetic induction, respectively. The key ingredient is a magnetic curl-jump penalty term, which allows us to prove a pre-asymptotic error estimate of order $O(h^{1/2})$ with a constant depending on solution norms but not explicitly on the fluid viscosity and magnetic diffusivity.
papers.title: A robust finite element method for incompressible magnetohydrodynamics using Whitney forms

papers.summary: We extend the Bourgain--Brézis--Mironescu (BBM) and Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova (MS) limit formulae to higher-order Besov norms on quantum Euclidean spaces $\R^d_θ$, a fundamental class of noncompact noncommutative manifolds obtained by deformation quantization of $\R^d$. A central ingredient is a Banach realization of the homogeneous Sobolev endpoint that forms a compatible couple with \(L_p(\R_θ^d)\), together with the equivalence \[ K\bigl(\x,\varepsilon^k; L_p(\R_θ^d),\dot W_{p,0}^k(\R_θ^d)\bigr) \approx ω_p^k(\x,\varepsilon). \] This framework yields a unified proof of both endpoint formulae through the endpoint continuity of real interpolation scales. The principal new ingredient at the MS endpoint is the sharp large-translation asymptotic \[ \lim_{|h|\to\infty}\|T_h\x-\x\|_p = 2^{1/p}\|\x\|_p, \qquad \x\in L_p(\R_θ^d),\quad 1\leq p<\infty, \] whose proof combines oscillatory decay of the non-pure terms in the tracial expansion with weighted spectral-measure arguments adapted to the semifinite trace.
papers.title: Limits of Besov Norms on Quantum Euclidean Spaces

papers.summary: In 1996, Michaux and Villemaire showed that any nontrivial expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +)$ defines new unary sets. We conjecture that the same holds over the structure $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$, and we prove a partial result in this direction. To do so, we first show that every nonempty sparse $k$-automatic set is a Presburger-definable image of some Cartesian power of $k^\mathbb{N}$. Using this characterization, we prove that if an expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$ defines the same unary sets, then every set of sublinear growth definable in the expansion is already definable in $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$.
papers.title: Sublinear Michaux-Villemaire over $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$

papers.summary: We establish a general result on the proof-theoretic strength of well-ordering principles in reverse mathematics. The novelty is that our result gives information over base theories as weak as $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, while previous results of Arai, Pakhomov-Walsh and Buriola-Weiermann required the stronger base theory $\mathsf{ACA}_0$. On the way, we strengthen a result of Carlucci-Mainardi-Rathjen about the ordinal analysis of theories of the form $\mathsf{RCA}_0+\text{``$α$ is a well-order"}$.
papers.title: Well-ordering principles over recursive comprehension

papers.summary: We establish a general decomposition for regular closed semilinear sets, derived from a detailed study of their topological boundary. As an application, we characterize stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces over an ordered field, extending previous results of Hoffmann, Tran, and Ye.
papers.title: On stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces

papers.summary: Let $S\subseteq \mathbb R^+$ be a subset of positive reals. We say that a metric space is an $S$-metric space if the range of the metric is a subset of $S\cup \{0\}$. In 2007, Delhommé, Laflamme, Pouzet, and Sauer characterized those sets $S$ for which the class of all finite $S$-metric spaces has the amalgamation property. Given an amalgamation class, a natural question is what its Ramsey expansion is. Ramsey expansions are known for classes of $S$-metric spaces for which $S\cup\{0\}$ carries a natural distance monoid structure, for example for $S=\mathbb Q^+$ or when $S$ is topologically closed. In this paper, we extend this result to all amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces, thereby completing the Ramsey-theoretic classification of amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces.
papers.title: Ramsey expansions of $S$-metric spaces

papers.summary: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.
papers.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras

papers.summary: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.
papers.title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings

papers.summary: Suppose that $r: X^2 \to X^2$ is a nondegenerate, involutive solution to the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation. To this data, we can associate an Artin--Schelter regular algebra $A$ and an infinite family of groups $G_k$, where $k \geqslant 1$. For each $k$, we show that $G_k$ is a dual reflection group for $A$, in the sense the component of $A$ graded by $1_{G_k}$ is again Artin--Schelter regular. We also show that, using the additional structure afforded by the underlying solution to the Yang--Baxter equation, one can determine the centre, Koszul complex, and associated twisted superpotential for $A$.
papers.title: Dual Reflection Groups from Solutions to the Yang--Baxter Equation

papers.summary: We present a proof for the $(n-2)$-linear extension estimate for curved surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge5$, at the local product exponent $2(n-1)/(n-2)^2$, with an arbitrarily small power loss. The hypotheses are transversality of the normals and nondegeneracy of the compressed shape operators on their common two-dimensional orthogonal complement. The argument combines polynomial partitioning, a descent through algebraic varieties, localized multilinear restriction, and positive packet-energy estimates.
papers.title: The $(n-2)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb R^n$

papers.summary: We describe the global structure of the self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$, without assuming properness or embeddedness. The main tool is a pair of piecewise monotone quantities along the profile curves, in the spirit of Hsiang's analysis of constant mean curvature hypersurfaces. We prove that every such self-shrinker other than the two invariant cylinders intersects both of them transversely, and all of them except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Apart from those of the cylinders, each end is either asymptotic to a cone or meets both cylinders infinitely many times. Consequently, a complete noncompact example is proper if and only if all its ends are asymptotically conical, and this is equivalent to polynomial volume growth, to finite entropy, and to finitely many intersections with the cylinders. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure, and for almost every initial condition the profile curve is either closed or generates a complete nonproper self-shrinker of infinite entropy. We also bound the winding of the profile curve by its number of cylinder crossings and localize its self-intersections.
papers.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-shrinkers

papers.summary: This paper deals with the naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras over the field of complex numbers. There are two finite series of such algebras, defined in every dimension starting from five, and two further algebras which occur only in dimension five. For each of these algebras we classify, up to isomorphism, all of its non-split central extensions, of every possible dimension. The one-dimensional central extensions are already known from an earlier work, so the main part of the paper is devoted to the extensions of dimension two and higher. As usual, the classification is reduced to the description of the orbits of the automorphism group of the algebra on the subspaces of its second cohomology space with trivial coefficients. For each algebra and each dimension we give the complete list of these orbits together with the multiplication tables of the corresponding algebras, and we point out the extensions whose annihilator coincides with the added central ideal. Among the algebras obtained there are 2-filiform Leibniz algebras which are not naturally graded; this class of algebras has not been systematically studied so far.
papers.title: Classification of all non-split central extensions of naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras

papers.summary: An infinite (binary) tree is \emph{positive} iff its set of paths is non-null. As an elementary observation, positives trees always have positive perfect subtrees. Given a positive tree of certain complexity, here we present several theorems concerning the distribution of the Turing jumps or iterated Turing jumps of (positive) perfect subtrees of the given tree in the universe of Turing degrees.
papers.title: Jumps and Iterated Jumps of Perfect Subtrees of Positive Trees
